lead_headline: AI SDK absorbs 33 commits as Zod 4.4 pressure and telemetry cleanup signal a stabilizing v5/v6 boundary
lead_body: AI SDK dominated Wednesday's commit log with parallel backports to v5 and v6, Zod 4.4 compatibility fixes, and a telemetry rename from onFinish to onEnd that suggests the instrumentation API is approaching a settled shape. Claude Code cut a minor release while its issue queue filled with agent-view edge cases — a zombie stop-hook loop, a silent AskUserQuestion dismissal, and leaking mouse-tracking sequences among them.
lead_article:
The busiest thread today runs through AI SDK, which absorbed 33 commits spanning bug fixes, documentation, and at least one feature of note: performance statistics landed via #15241, and a telemetry rename — onFinish to onEnd — suggests the instrumentation layer is being tidied toward a stable shape. Two Zod-related fixes arrived in close succession, one correcting validateUIMessages against Zod 4.4 and another through the backport channel, which hints at downstream pressure from users already on newer Zod versions. The sandbox feature was quietly demoted to experimental, and the open-responses provider now maps non-image file parts to input_file rather than dropping them. Backports to both the v5 and v6 release branches ran in parallel throughout the afternoon, which is the SDK's usual release cadence made visible.

Astro shipped five packages — astro@6.3.2 among them — and a PR opened late in the evening adds Cloudflare fetch and Hono handler exports for advanced routing, which is the more forward-looking movement. Claude Code cut v2.1.141 but the release itself is minor; the issue queue tells the more interesting story: a zombie-subagent stop-hook loop, an AskUserQuestion card that silently resolves as dismissed on app quit, and mouse-tracking escape sequences leaking into prompt input all arrived today, suggesting the agent-view rollout is surfacing edge cases faster than the patch cycle can absorb them. Workflow SDK opened three PRs, the most substantive being region-aware queue routing and a new World.createRunId() method, while Gemma.cpp saw a PR removing Q-matrix transposition from the tiled attention kernel — a low-profile change that touches numerics.
